title: Common providers: Thailand
coverage: Partial. Covers the national carriers, the mobile network operators, the main fibre broadband name and five business ISPs; names are given in Latin script, as the providers write them on their own pages.
missing: Names in Thai script (none was confirmed against a source that may be copied)
The regulator's operator register (the NBTC site refused an automated check on the read date, and it is in Thai)
Smaller business ISPs and regional operators
Websites for NT, INET and UniNet (none answered an automated check on the read date)
Status pages (none was found that answered a check)
A website for UIH (it answered an automated request only with a refusal or a bot check on the read date)

sources.name: NBTC (National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission)
sources.terms: The site refused an automated check on the read date, so its terms were not read and nothing is taken.
sources.result: Did not answer (HTTP 403). It is the authority to consult for operators this pack lacks.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Internet in Thailand and Telecommunications in Thailand
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Used to cross-check names and ownership (facts); no text is copied.
sources.result: 9 of 10 names were found on the pages.

sources.name: Each provider's own public website
sources.terms: Only the address itself is recorded (a fact); no content is copied.
sources.result: 6 of 10 websites and 2 business, support or status pages answered an automated check; an address that did not answer is left empty. An address that answered only with a refusal, a bot check or a page-not-found page counts as one that did not answer.

sources.name: RIPEstat as-overview (RIPE NCC)
sources.terms: The RIPEstat service terms were read on the read date; RIPEstat data is not redistributed: nothing is copied. Consulted to confirm, for each AS number, the registered holder and that the number is announced.
sources.result: 24 AS numbers confirmed; a number whose registered holder was another company, or that was not announced on the read date, was left out.

sources.name: NRO delegated statistics (the regional registries' joint list of assigned AS numbers)
sources.terms: Published by the registries for public use; only which registry holds each AS number is taken (a fact).
sources.result: Every AS number in the pack was found in the list; its registry is recorded beside it.

sources.name: PeeringDB
sources.terms: The acceptable use policy forbids reproducing PeeringDB data outside approved operational purposes: nothing is copied; cited as a place to look up an AS number.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Advanced Info Service
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Cited for names and dates (facts); no text is copied.
sources.result: Read on the date above: Triple T Broadband (3BB) is listed as a subsidiary of AIS.

providers.name: AIS
providers.notes: Mobile and fibre. The numbers are registered to its companies Advanced Wireless Network and Super Broadband Network. Triple T Broadband (3BB) is its subsidiary and is listed apart.

providers.name: True
providers.notes: Mobile, fibre and cable; merged with dtac (AS24378, still registered to Total Access Communication). The second address is dtac's.

providers.name: 3BB
providers.notes: Fibre broadband; the trading name of Triple T Broadband, a subsidiary of AIS. It is listed apart, with its own AS numbers.

providers.name: NT
providers.notes: The merged CAT Telecom and TOT (AS23969 and AS38040 are still registered to TOT). Its website did not answer an automated check.

providers.name: INET
providers.notes: Its website refused an automated check on the read date.

providers.name: UniNet
providers.notes: The universities' network. Its website did not answer an automated check on the read date.
